headline: Interactive Sentence Order Game for Grammar Practice
outcomes: Students internalize English word order by physically arranging scrambled words into correct sentences
Build awareness of grammatical structure — subjects, verbs, objects, and modifiers — through active construction
Develop reading accuracy by processing each word's grammatical role rather than guessing from context
Practice a range of sentence types including questions, negatives, and complex clauses
howItWorks: The AI generates a sentence on the chosen topic, then scrambles the words into random order
Students tap words on their device to build the sentence in the correct sequence
The game validates placement in real time — students see which words are correctly positioned
Faster, accurate completions earn more points; the teacher sees all responses on the classroom board
teacherUseCases: Grammar point practice after introducing a new structure — conditionals, passive voice, question forms
Reading warmup that activates syntactic awareness before a text-based lesson
Formative check to see which sentence patterns students find most difficult

faq.q: Can I target a specific grammar point?
faq.a: Yes. The difficulty setting shapes sentence complexity. For specific structures, set the topic to something like 'present perfect sentences' and the AI will generate sentences that feature that grammar point.
Easy mode uses 4–6 word sentences suitable for beginners. Medium is 6–8 words and hard uses 8–12 words with more complex structures including embedded clauses.

faq.q: Is there an app students need to install?
faq.a: No app needed. Students open the session in their mobile browser — they tap the link the teacher shares and they're in. Works on any modern phone or tablet.

faq.q: What happens if students get stuck?
faq.a: There's no penalty for taking longer — students still complete the round. The teacher can also reveal the correct sentence for discussion.

faq.q: Is the content pre-made or AI-generated?
faq.a: Fully AI-generated on demand. Every session pulls fresh sentences matched to your topic, so content never feels stale or repeated.
Yes, Sentence Scramble is free to try. No student accounts are needed — students join through a browser link in seconds.
